  allows; run rows support viewing, filtering, artifact/evidence opening, resume/retry where valid, clone-as-new-run,
  export, and raw/ledger inspection. Compare versions is deep in MVP with rendered output, package/source-lineage
  metadata, source ledger atom lineage where applicable, and manifest identity. Export actions support selected
  rows, multi-select bundles, filtered views, zip/archive, JSON, rendered Markdown, rendered HTML, rendered PDF,
  and explicit evidence/redaction profiles. When projection state is stale, compare/export/reopen/send-forward remain
  blocked until Rebuild succeeds.

items.impact: Resume, retry, clone, duplicate, rebuild, and send-forward can acquire inconsistent identities or mutate authority-bearing state without auditable semantics.
items.statement: OP-027 enumerates open, compare, duplicate, reopen, export, send-forward, resume, retry, clone, and rebuild behavior without command IDs, payload/result schemas, idempotency, authorization snapshots, confirmation levels, disabled-reason enums, or receipt effects.
items.title: History actions have labels but no command and receipt contracts

evidence.exact_quote:
and explicit evidence/redaction profiles. When projection state is stale, compare/export/reopen/send-forward remain
  blocked until Rebuild succeeds.

items.impact: A rebuild can lose new history, publish a mixed generation, or unlock actions against data that became stale during reconstruction.
items.statement: Rebuild is a visible gate for four actions, but the specification does not define its immutable input snapshot, handling of events arriving during rebuild, temporary generation, atomic swap, failure cleanup, cancellation, version proof, or whether a successful rebuild can already be stale.
items.title: Rebuild has no atomicity, concurrency, or rollback algorithm

evidence.exact_quote:
- Do not silently include raw records or evidence in ordinary exports.
- Do not export secrets, unauthorized provider/account details, or evidence outside the user's permissions.
- Do not omit a manifest of redactions/omissions when evidence export is requested.

items.impact: Zip, JSON, HTML, PDF, and evidence exports can leak provider credentials, account details, raw payloads, or removed material despite displaying a redaction option.
items.statement: The source requires explicit profiles and omission manifests but gives no profile schema, secret classes, field-level policy, viewer/exporter distinction, encryption, archive integrity, size limit, cancellation cleanup, or test fixture for forbidden data.
items.title: Evidence export privacy requirements lack a concrete enforcement contract

evidence.exact_quote: Orchestrator command exposure for recovery and navigation is route-open only into owner surfaces, while runtime mutation recovery maps through ordered allowed_action_ids to cmd.runtime commands.

- Repairs `sfk-4ac2b9911ffce6c6ae062b08`: safe-point retry UI shows action `cmd.orchestrator.safe_point_retry` with fields `run_id`, `safe_point_id`, `retry_scope`, and `permission_snapshot_id?`. Confirmation copy must name the safe point and affected node/run. Disabled reasons are `safe_point_missing`, `state_changed`, `permission_denied`, and `operation_in_progress`.

items.impact: The page may mint a panel-local runtime mutation, creating two command authorities and inconsistent permission/receipt behavior.
items.statement: The owner-routing PlanUnit says runtime mutation recovery maps to cmd.runtime commands, but the later repair addendum defines cmd.orchestrator.safe_point_retry as the retry action without explaining a route-only wrapper or superseding the earlier authority rule.
items.title: Safe-point retry command conflicts with runtime mutation ownership

items.impact: Audits and builders can alternately treat the DAG action contract as closed or unresolved, defeating deterministic readiness and repair accounting.
items.statement: The addendum says the core DAG command row is repaired with concrete IDs and enablement, while the adjacent audit-lineage note for the same sfk says it is explicitly deferred and requires a dedicated lane; the note is also visibly truncated. evidence.exact_quote: Orchestrator usage, cost, ledger, evidence, history, and receipt rows are consumers of UsageRecord projection packets. They display source_class, source_confidence, source_authority, settlement_status, cost_status, quota_state, projection_freshness, projection_health, hidden/background contribution, and dedupe/parent-child refs when usage appears in a row or detail panel. `View in Usage`, `Show in Usage`, and `Show in Ledger` actions route through object_kind = usage_event and object_id from usage_event_ref whenever present, preserving usage_record_id, provider_attempt_ref, attempt_id, node_id, tool_call_id, trace_ref, receipt refs, raw_payload_ref, artifact_id, run_id, and thread_id as correlation/context fields.

items.impact: A consumer may fall back to an ambiguous timestamp/run key or reveal raw billing/provider material to a viewer who can see the summary row but not the source record.
items.statement: OP-029 normalizes routes when usage_event_ref is present and preserves raw_payload_ref plus provider/account correlation, but does not define disabled/fallback behavior when the primary ref is absent or authorization/redaction when opening raw payload and sensitive provider details.
items.title: Usage drill-through has no safe fallback or raw-payload authorization rule

evidence.exact_quote: - Hidden/background usage contribution is attributed through parent_usage_record_id or child usage refs rather than silently folded into parent-only totals.

items.impact: Background/subagent costs can be counted twice, disappear during settlement updates, or create recursive drill-through and unbounded traversal.
items.statement: OP-029 requires parent/child drill-through but gives no acyclicity, dedupe-key, streaming partial-to-final replacement, adjustment/reversal, aggregation, or maximum-depth rule.
items.title: Usage parent-child attribution lacks cycle and double-count rules
